prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” roofer for every homeowner — the best choice depends on your needs (fast insurance help, lifetime warranty, lowest price, etc.). Instead of one name, it’s safer to pick a Denver roofer with the right credentials, strong local reviews, hail‑damage experience, and reliable insurance/permit handling.

How to find the best roofer for hail damage in Denver
- Check credentials and affiliations
  - GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, or Owens Corning Platinum/Preferred contractors — these manufacturer certifications mean training and enhanced warranties.
  - Colorado/local city contractor registration or building department records (some municipalities require permits/registration).
  - General liability and workers’ comp insurance — get copies of certificates.

- Look at local reputation
  - Google Reviews, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Yelp, and BBB ratings. Prefer contractors with many recent positive reviews for hail repair.
  - Ask for local references from homeowners who had hail claims in the last 12–24 months.

- Verify hail/insurance experience
  - Choose a roofer experienced with insurance claims who will document damage (photos, measurements, Xactimate or similar estimates) and can work with adjusters without being a “storm chaser.”

- Ask about warranties and materials
  - Distinguish material warranties (manufacturer) vs. workmanship warranties (contractor). Get both in writing.
  - Ask whether they replace vs. patch, and what shingle brand and class they use.

- Get multiple detailed estimates
  - Obtain at least 2–3 written estimates that list materials, scope, tear‑off vs. overlay, permit handling, debris cleanup, and warranty terms.
  - Compare scope and line items, not just final price.

Key questions to ask a roofer
- How many hail‑damage roofs have you repaired in Denver in the last year?
- Are you certified by shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
- Will you provide a written scope, permit fee breakdown, and timeline?
- Do you handle insurance claims and meet with adjusters? Do you charge extra for that?
- What are your workmanship and material warranties? Get them in writing.
- Can you provide 3 local references and photos of recent hail jobs?

Red flags to avoid
- Door‑to‑door high‑pressure sales right after a storm (possible storm chasers).
- Demanding large upfront cash payment or paying in full before work starts.
- No local address or poor/no references.
- No proof of insurance or refusal to provide certificates.
- Very low bid with vague scope — likely to add charges later or cut corners.

Resources to find contractors
- GAF / CertainTeed dealer locators (search for Master Elite / SELECT contractors)
- Google Maps + reviews
- BBB and Angi/HomeAdvisor
- Local Facebook neighborhood groups or Nextdoor for recent homeowner recommendations

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated hail-repair roofers near you if you give your Denver zip code or neighborhood.
- Provide a checklist you can print for contractor visits and estimate comparisons.

Which would you prefer — a short list of Denver roofers near you, or the printable checklist and sample questions to take to estimates?
